newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: YUGO TO ALLOW 60-DAY ADVANCE IMPORT PAYMENTS.
newsitem.headline: YUGO TO ALLOW 60-DAY ADVANCE IMPORT PAYMENTS.

text.p: Yugoslavia will allow advance payments for imports, but goods must arrive in the country within 60 days of payment or face high fines, the Official Gazzette said on Wednesday.

"Contracts for advance sale of imported goods have to be registered with the National Bank of Yugoslavia, and goods have to arrive within 60 days from payment to the foreign partner," the Yugoslav government said in its regulation published in the Gazzette.

If goods do not arrive in time, importers will be fined double the amount of the dinar equivalent of the imports at the exchange rate valid on the date of the expiration of the 60-day term, the regulation said.
The law could help prevent businesses from feigning contracts just to move foreign exchange out of the country.

Advance import payments can be made on raw materials, spare-parts, medicine and medical supplies, software, industrial ownership rights, know-how, experience, film screening rights and import-related services, the Gazette said. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom 381 11 311 43 05
